newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Colombo crepe prices rise over shortage fears.
newsitem.headline: Colombo crepe prices rise over shortage fears.

text.p: Crepe prices rose at the Colombo auction on Thursday because of fears of short supply due to forthcoming holidays and drought, exporters and brokers said.
"Sri Lanka's crepe market seems to be having problems due to drought," said an exporter. "So there's a little pressure on shippers who need to fulfill their contracts before the holidays."
Prices were likely to hold because tapping will be interrupted in the runup to, and after, the April 13-14 traditional new year celebrations, he said.

Best latex one-x, the purest grade, rose to 77.75 rupees ($1.33) per kg from 76.25 on Tuesday when the auction was last held, brokers said. Latex crepe number one rose to 77.25 rupees per kg from 75.50 while RSS 1 was unquoted on both days.
Brokers said 314 tonnes of crepe, 63 tonnes of scrap crepe and 16 tonnes of sheet were on offer.
Tropical Sri Lanka is experiencing a drought after the November-March northeast monsoon failed for a second year in a row.
